extracted.intended_audience: NIH SBIR/STTR applicants and grant writers (small-business biomedical investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required sections for preparing an NIH SBIR/STTR (PA-16-302) grant application, including required Research Plan components, budget justification, SBIR/STTR-specific questions, and study-specific validation/approach expectations for a biomedical project (antibody:antigen epitope mapping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims (aims_PA-16-302.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A one-page statement of the research objectives and distinct aims. Example in this application: Aim 1 — Define communities of antibodies with similar antigen binding patterns; Aim 2 — Localize antibody epitopes. Should articulate what will be accomplished and why it matters (scoped for the FOA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy — Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy A. Significance: explain importance of the problem, how the project fills a gap, and the broader impacts on vaccines/therapeutics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate why characterization of antibody:antigen binding and epitope localization matter; cite limitations of existing methods (e.g., x-ray/cryo-EM too slow/expensive, alanine scanning low hit rate) and argue how the proposed approach addresses those gaps. Provide biological rationale (e.g., HSV vaccine trial results) and potential health/clinical impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy — Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy B. Innovation: describe novel aspects of the project and how it departs from current practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific innovations (as in the proposal): integration of computational docking with large-scale binding studies; computational design of mutation sets (beyond alanine scans); exploitation of natural and artificial antigenic variability; systematic analysis of antibody competition across multiple antigens; development of reference panels; new computational analysis methods for large-scale antibody competition and binding studies. Explain how these innovations overcome limitations of prior methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy — Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy C. Approach: detail experimental/computational methods, study design, preliminary data, and analysis plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe complementary approaches (e.g., binning-based inference for communities; binding-based inference for fine localization), experimental matrices (antibody vs antibody competition; antibody vs antigen binding matrices), how data will be analyzed, validation plan (retrospective tests against low-throughput data and prospective prediction validated by x-ray crystallography), and practical execution (use of Wasatch SPR, computational modeling, designed antigen variants). Include figures/intuition and plans to interpret competition/binding matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of the Premise / Rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Strength of the Premise: justify the scientific rationale and feasibility of the underlying hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence that the combined experimental-computational approach is plausible (e.g., Wasatch SPR provides rich data; existing low-throughput 'ground truth' data for HSV gD). Compare with alternative methods and explain why the premise is strong enough to warrant the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation and Testing Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed plan to test methods retrospectively and prospectively and to validate predictions by higher-resolution structural methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retrospective testing against existing low-throughput data; prospective prediction of binding and binding modes to be confirmed by x-ray crystallography. Validation expectations are part of demonstrating feasibility and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Appropriate Instrumentation and Platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate availability and suitability of high-throughput instrumentation (Wasatch SPR and Continuous Flow Microspotter) for the proposed experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the Wasatch multiplexed SPR and CFM/CFM-derived data enable the proposed large-scale analyses; include instrument throughput, features (e.g., planned 384-spot improvement) and past commercialization history as evidence of capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team Qualifications and Collaborative Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Team and Outlook: describe complementary expertise and plans for collaboration among investigators and external collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify roles (e.g., computational lead, experimental system lead, instrument lead), collaborations (e.g., structural validation at Pasteur Institute, variant generation by Integral Molecular), and statements of contribution in Letters of Support. Demonstrate that the team has necessary expertise and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Research Plan required sections
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS 398 Research Plan: required components and file attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required sections listed: Introduction (for resubmission/revision), Specific Aims, Research Strategy (Research_Plan-v4.5_PA-16-302.pdf), Progress Report Publication List, Protection of Human Subjects, Data Safety Monitoring Plan, Inclusion of Women and Minorities, Inclusion of Children, Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan (MultiPI_Leadership_Plan_PA-16-302.pdf), Consortium/Contractual Arrangements, Letters of Support (Letters_of_Support_2016_NIH_-_PA-16-302.pdf), Resource Sharing Plan(s), Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources, Appendix. Follow FOA and PHS 398 instructions for each section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects protections and clinical trial designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Subjects Section: indicate whether the project involves human subjects and/or a clinical trial; include Protection of Human Subjects and Data Safety Monitoring Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer 'Clinical Trial?' and 'Agency-Defined Phase III Clinical Trial?'; provide protection and monitoring plans, inclusion plans for women/minorities/children. These elements are required and will affect review and regulatory oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals reporting and AVMA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertebrate Animals Section: state whether vertebrate animals are euthanized and, if so, whether the method is consistent with AVMA guidelines (or justify otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If euthanasia is used, indicate compliance with AVMA; if not consistent, provide method description and scientific justification. This is a required disclosure in PHS 398.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Embryonic Stem Cells reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Embryonic Stem Cells Section: state whether project involves hESCs and provide registry numbers or state that a registry line will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hESCs are used, list the registration number(s) from the NIH registry or indicate that one from the registry will be used. This is a compliance requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and Patents disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions and Patents Section: disclose whether inventions/patents arise from the project and whether previously reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer yes/no and provide details if yes; necessary for reporting and IP management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget structure and required budget elements
rubrics_metrics.description: RESEARCH & RELATED Budget sections A-K: specify personnel (Section A/B), equipment (C), travel (D), participant support (E), other direct costs (F), direct costs (G), indirect costs (H), total costs (I), and fee (J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cumulative and period budgets; list equipment items (see equipment threshold), materials and supplies, publication costs, consultant services, ADP/computer services, subawards, facility rental/user fees, alterations, and other. Attach Budget Justification (single file). Ensure calculations for total direct and indirect costs are correct and reflect FOA rules (e.g., excluding consortium F&A when applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment listing threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: List items and dollar amount for each equipment item exceeding $5,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide equipment item descriptions and funds requested for each item > $5,000 and attach additional equipment file if necessary. Total equipment must be shown in Section C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification / Personnel Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget Justification attachment (e.g., Dartmouth_Personnel_Justification.pdf) describing personnel roles, effort, and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe each key person's percentage effort (calendar months), specific responsibilities (e.g., Dr. Cairns: high-throughput epitope dissection; Doina Atanasiu: day-to-day glycoprotein characterization; Huan Lou: protein production and purification), and justify salaries and fringe. For senior/key persons, provide base salary, months, requested salary, and fringe benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost rate disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect Cost Type and Indirect Cost Rate (%) with base and funds requested (Section H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the institutional indirect cost rate and base; example given: '62% of Dartmouth total direct - equip' — include cognizant federal agency and POC info. Ensure consistency with institutional negotiated rate agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR-specific certifications and questions (Questions 1-7)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR Information — Questions 1-7 must be completed by all SBIR and STTR applicants (program type, phase, small business eligibility, anticipated personnel, subcontracts with federal labs, HUBZone, US performance of R&D, prior equivalent work, disclosure permission, commercialization plan for Phase II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Program Type (SBIR/STTR/Both) and Phase (I/II/Fast-Track). Certify small business eligibility and anticipated employee count. Disclose subcontracts with Federal labs. State HUBZone status. State whether all R&D will be performed in the US (if no, provide explanation). Disclose previous submissions/awards for equivalent work. Indicate government permission to disclose applicant contact info if not funded. Attach commercialization plan for Phase II or Fast-Track as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR-specific questions (8-9)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR Questions 8-9 apply only to SBIR: history of prior SBIR Phase II awards and whether PD/PI will have primary employment with the small business at time of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior Phase II awards exist, provide commercialization history attachment (example: Wasatch_Microfluidics_Commercialization_History.pdf). State PD/PI primary employment status with the small business at award time.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR-specific questions (10-11)
rubrics_metrics.description: STTR Questions 10-11 apply only to STTR: PD/PI formal appointment/commitment and devotion of at least 10% effort; distribution of work (small business >=40%, research institution >=30%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer whether both conditions for PD/PI appointment and effort are true and whether the small business and research institution proportions of work meet STTR requirements. These determine STTR eligibility and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium/Contractual Arrangements and Letters of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Consortium/Contractual Arrangements (Section 12) and Letters of Support (Section 13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide formal letters describing commitments, roles, and in-kind support (e.g., Pasteur collaboration letter describing facilities and access to crystallogenesis core and synchrotron beam time). Letters should demonstrate collaborator capabilities and access to necessary resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing and Authentication plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource Sharing Plan(s) and Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources (Section 14 & 15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for data/material sharing (e.g., sequences, reagents) and procedures to authenticate cell lines, antibodies, reagents, and other key resources to ensure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Development Outside the U.S. justification
rubrics_metrics.description: If any R&D will be performed outside the U.S., provide explanation and documentation (e.g., letters showing collaborator capacity and access to facilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach explanations and collaboration letters; demonstrate that foreign collaborators have required facilities and expertise (example: Pasteur letter describing crystallography capabilities and beam time access).
